Markus / Monica,

Thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Quick summary of how we handle these at Redwood:

1) Default payment term for new vendor activations is Net 45. We moved from Net 30 last year to help standardize month-end runs across multiple regions.

2) Exceptions: Net 30 or Net 30 with early-pay discounts can be approved on a case-by-case basis. Finance (Monica) owns the exception workflow; approvals require:
   - Completed onboarding form + W9 (received)
   - Procurement justification (volume forecast / strategic reasons)
   - A signed amendment to the Master Vendor Agreement (MVA) if there0s a discount or fee structure change

3) Early-pay program: we currently run a small pilot for strategic suppliers. Typical structures:
   - 2% discount for payment within 10 business days (Net 10/Net 15)
   - 1% discount or 0.75% fee for accelerated payment to Net 30
   - Alternatively, an "expedite" charge (0.5% flat) that Finance collects and remits internally

4) PO header requirements for the vendor portal: remit name, legal entity, tax id (EIN), invoice routing code (4-digit), and correct bill-to address. I0ve attached the example PO_template_example.xlsx for their team to see the exact fields.

Next steps I recommend:
- Monica: please confirm whether we can make an exception for Sable to Net 30 or enroll them in the early-pay pilot. If yes, we0ll need an amendment (I can coordinate with Legal).
- Markus: confirm whether Sales is comfortable passing along an early-pay option to the vendor (discount vs fee).

I0ll also update the vendor portal record to show Net 45 as the default until we get an exception approved.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference

Markus / Priyom,

Appreciate the context. Given the spend profile (estimated $120k in 6 months) and that Sable is a strategic engineering partner, I recommend the following path:

1) Default activation: set Sable to Net 45 in the vendor portal now so invoices flow into our standard AR run. I will update the portal record (vendor id 5678).
2) Offer a limited early-pay pilot: Net 30 with a 1% early-pay credit if Redwood pays within 15 calendar days. This is lower than their ask for Net 15/2% but balances cashflow and cost.
3) Requirements before pilot:
   - Signed amendment to the MVA outlining the pilot dates (90 days initial) and the credit mechanics (accounting to apply credit at payment time).
   - Procurement forecast (Markus please capture expected monthly volumes in the portal comment).
   - Finance will validate the budget impact and provide final sign-off within 3 business days after amendment is received.

I0ll draft the amendment and loop in Legal; Priyom, please add the PO header notes to the vendor portal and ensure the PO_template_example.xlsx is attached to the vendor record. Markus, if Sales confirms expected volumes in the portal comment, we can turn the pilot on the same day the amendment is signed.

Monica Patel
